title: Zero transfer on mixed graphs
abstract: In this paper, we investigate zero transfer on mixed graphs. Zero transfer is a quantum walk phenomenon in which the transition amplitude between two vertices is identically zero for all times, so that no quantum state transfer occurs between them. Using the Hermitian adjacency matrix, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for zero transfer in mixed graphs. We then specialize these criteria to oriented circulant graphs, obtaining nonexistence results for prime order, structural restrictions for even order, and exhaustive computational classifications for small orders.
summary: This paper develops rigorous mathematical criteria to determine when a quantum state transfer between two nodes on a mixed graph is impossible (zero transfer). It achieves this by analyzing the spectral properties of the graph's Hermitian adjacency matrix, providing specific nonexistence results for prime-ordered circulant graphs and detailed classifications for composite orders.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the phenomenon of 'zero transfer'—where quantum state transition amplitudes vanish for all time—on mixed graphs.
main_result: Zero transfer is characterized by vanishing entries in the spectral idempotents associated with the graph's Hermitian adjacency matrix. For oriented circulant graphs of prime order, zero transfer cannot occur.
method: The analysis uses advanced linear algebra techniques, including Taylor series expansions and spectral decomposition theorems applied to quantum walks governed by a Hermitian Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The model is a continuous-time quantum walk on a mixed graph $\Gamma$, whose evolution is dictated by the Hermitian adjacency matrix $H_\Gamma$. The system involves both undirected edges and directed arcs.

important_parameters: Graph order ($n$), primality of $n$, and the specific connectivity defined by the generating set $C$ in circulant graphs.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the properties of Hermitian matrices, spectral decomposition, and algebraic number theory related to roots of unity when analyzing circulant structures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an example of zero transfer for a specific mixed graph $G(\mathbb{Z}_{12}, \{2, 3, 8\})$, showing the set of vertices exhibiting this property. Tables summarize counts and sets for various small even orders ($n \le 20$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from general necessary conditions (Taylor expansion) to more precise spectral characterizations (spectral idempotents), culminating in detailed case studies on oriented circulant graphs, especially analyzing the prime vs. composite order cases.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical tools for understanding quantum transport phenomena, which are foundational to designing robust quantum communication channels or characterizing decoherence mechanisms in complex quantum systems.
